# gut

> Judgment calls as one line of Python, on small, fast, cheap models. Write a decision that is
> judgment rather than logic -- "is this spam?", "which team owns this?" -- as one readable line,
> say how careful to be in words instead of thresholds, and get back YES, NO or UNSURE. Built around
> TypeSafe AI's Jev, and model-agnostic: a local NLI encoder, a local 0.6B LLM or any
> OpenAI-compatible server answer the same line.

Python 3.10+, Apache-2.0. `pip install gutfeel` (the PyPI name; the import is `import gut`), plus
`gutfeel[local]` for in-process models, `gutfeel[jev]` for Jev or `gutfeel[mcp]` for the MCP server.
The documentation is also published at https://kungie.github.io/gut/docs/.

## Start here

- [SKILL.md](skills/gut/SKILL.md): the compact usage guide. Correct spellings, the traps, the rules
  of thumb, and which backend to pick. Read this one if you are writing code that uses gut.
- [README.md](README.md): the pitch. What problem this solves and what it looks like.
- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md): the full guide, one page per idea.

## Reference

- [docs/backends.md](docs/backends.md): every backend, how each one reads a model's probabilities,
  `Cascade`, and writing your own.
- [docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md): `gut filter` and `gut map`, judgments over lines of text from a shell,
  with a cost summary and `--max-cost`.
- [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md): `gutfeel-mcp`, the same judgments as MCP tools (`likely`, `classify`,
  `rate`, `each`) for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients.
- [examples/](examples/): the same handlers on any backend, chosen with `--backend`.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to run the suite.

## The parts, in one line each

- `likely(subject, question)` — a yes/no judgment. `classify(subject, EnumClass)` — which one.
  `rate(subject, levels)` — how much.
- `stakes` / `lean` / `ask_human` — how careful to be, in words. Maps onto a cost model.
- `cost_false_yes` / `cost_false_no` / `cost_human` — the same thing in numbers, when you know them.
- `each(subjects).likely(...)` — the same question about many subjects, in as few calls as possible.
- `@semantic` and `judge()` — every judgment about one subject, handed to the model together.
- `alikely` / `aclassify` / `arate`, `each(...).alikely(...)`, `judge.aresolve()` — the same, awaitable.
- `JevBackend` — TypeSafe's Jev, the default. `ZeroShotBackend`, `TransformersBackend` — models in
  your process. `OpenAICompatibleBackend` — Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenAI.
- `Cascade(small, bigger)` — the cheap model first; only unsure answers go on.
- `FakeBackend` — develop and test with no model at all.
- `configure(on_decision=...)` and `decision.to_dict()` — see every decision as it is made.
- `usage(max_cost=...)` — count calls and dollars; past the budget the next call raises `BudgetExceeded`.
- `JevBackend.openrouter()` — Jev through OpenRouter, which reports the price of every call.

## Traps worth knowing before you write any code

- `case gut.YES:` must be dotted. A bare `case YES:` is a capture pattern and does not compile.
- `ask_human=True` is required for `UNSURE` to be possible at all.
- Posture words and exact costs cannot be mixed in one call.
- `cost_human` above `cfy * cfn / (cfy + cfn)` makes `UNSURE` unreachable; gut warns.
- `confidence` is a spread statistic, not a probability of being correct.
- `OpenAICompatibleBackend` needs logprobs: not OpenAI's reasoning models.
- Text-model backends take at most 26 options in a `classify`.
- One claim per question: an NLI model reads "A or B" poorly.
